summary: Krea-2 + the first-party darkbrush LoRA. Monochrome ink wash: near-black masses on near-white paper, ink spatter, silhouette-driven. Ryan 2026-08-12: 'this one could translate really well to video.'
graphStatus: NOT WRITTEN YET — export from ComfyUI's official Krea-2 template on the first box.
triggerNote: Krea LoRAs are trigger-phrase driven. Append it to the END of the scene text, per the model card's own examples ('A deer grazing in the forest, monochrome ink wash style').
vramNote: ESTIMATE. 12.2GB model + 4.9GB text encoder + activations. Measure on first run and replace.
baseNote: TURBO is the default, on evidence: the LoRA's HF tags say base_model:krea/Krea-2-Turbo and every published preview is named *_turbo. The model card TEXT claims Krea-2-Raw — the card and the tags disagree, and the tags plus the preview filenames are the stronger signal. Which base it was actually trained against remains UNVERIFIED.

rawVariant.note: The A/B. Same seed, raw vs turbo, Ryan picks. Sharing the turbo base with krea2-linen-scroll also puts both LoRAs on ONE box; switching this to raw splits them across two.

whyVideo: Temporal stability comes from the style's shape, not from the video model: value extremes rather than mid-tones (less to flicker), almost no high-frequency texture (nothing to re-derive per frame), stochastic spatter (variation reads as intentional), silhouette compositions, and monochrome (colour drift cannot occur). The style enters at the KEYFRAME and Wan follows it — there is no video LoRA involved.
costs: Monochrome. keyframes-v10's approved look carries muted colour with one saturated accent; this drops all of it. And the sample mood is dramatic (samurai, wraiths, lightning) against Ryan's deadpan material — tonal mismatch is the risk samples cannot reveal.
